Jul 31Medium-low confidenceoutbound · 06:00–22:00 ET
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.NWS-hrNWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. This day is already covered by finer-resolution sources.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

Extended outlook summary

(Wednesday night through Monday) Issued at 531 AM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026 Into mid-week the ridge begins to push back to the west and break down a tad pushing our area into a more dry pattern Wednesday through Friday.

Short term

.. (Today through Wednesday) Issued at 531 AM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026 The big story in the short term will be today's heat. Afternoon highs will climb into the upper 80s across the CWA and with dewpoints in the 70's we'll have no issue reaching heat advisory criteria for all of the CWA outside of the highest elevations of NE Georgia. The heat is no joke, please exercise extreme caution if decide to spend the afternoon outside. We'll be monitoring the potential for another MCS embedded in the NW flow this afternoon. High res models continue to keep the worst of it off to the east of us or falling apart before it reaches us. These NW flow systems can be tricky to forecast tracks for but the best chance to see thunderstorms tomorrow remains across eastern Georgia. If the system holds together or the track shifts to include more of our CWA the main threat will be damaging winds. A heat advisory will likely be needed again tomorrow for the portion of the CWA south of a line from Columbus to Macon and along the I-16 corridor. The northern CWA should expect to see drier air filter in that will gradually bring relief from high heat indices CWA wide by

Long term

.. (Wednesday night through Monday) Issued at 531 AM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026 Into mid-week the ridge begins to push back to the west and break down a tad pushing our area into a more dry pattern Wednesday through Friday. With the drier air in place, dewpoints will be quite pleasant in the low 60s across the area by Friday afternoon.Temps will also top out in the upper 80s to low 90s across the area. Pushing into the weekend a trough swings down into the TN/KY area which will in turn push in a frontal boundary during this time period which increases rain chances Saturday through Monday. Too early to determine a severe risk if any but will be keeping an eye on this system as it tracks into our area. Temperatures will continue to be pleasant into the weekend with highs most days in the mid to upper 80s.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Peachtree City GA
640 AM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026



...New 12Z Aviation Discussion...

.KEY MESSAGES...

  - The threat for storms will continue late today into Wednesday
    morning with the main threats being gusty winds, locally heavy
    rainfall, and frequent lightning across north and eastern 
    Georgia.

  - Heat index values exceeding 105 degrees are forecast on
    Tuesday. A Heat Advisory has been issued for nearly all of
    north and central Georgia for Tuesday afternoon and evening.

  - Drier conditions are forecast across north and central Georgia
    on Thursday and Friday.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Wednesday)
Issued at 531 AM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026

The big story in the short term will be today's heat. Afternoon 
highs will climb into the upper 80s across the CWA and with 
dewpoints in the 70's we'll have no issue reaching heat advisory 
criteria for all of the CWA outside of the highest elevations of NE 
Georgia. The heat is no joke, please exercise extreme caution if 
decide to spend the afternoon outside. 

We'll be monitoring the potential for another MCS embedded in the NW 
flow this afternoon. High res models continue to keep the worst of 
it off to the east of us or falling apart before it reaches us. 
These NW flow systems can be tricky to forecast tracks for but the 
best chance to see thunderstorms tomorrow remains across eastern 
Georgia. If the system holds together or the track shifts to include 
more of our CWA the main threat will be damaging winds. 

A heat advisory will likely be needed again tomorrow for the portion 
of the CWA south of a line from Columbus to Macon and along the I-16 
corridor. The northern CWA should expect to see drier air filter in 
that will gradually bring relief from high heat indices CWA wide by 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Wednesday night through Monday)
Issued at 531 AM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Into mid-week the ridge begins to push back to the west and break 
down a tad pushing our area into a more dry pattern Wednesday 
through Friday. With the drier air in place, dewpoints will be quite 
pleasant in the low 60s across the area by Friday afternoon.Temps 
will also top out in the upper 80s to low 90s across the area. 
Pushing into the weekend a trough swings down into the TN/KY area 
which will in turn push in a frontal boundary during this time period 
which increases rain chances Saturday through Monday. Too early to 
determine a severe risk if any but will be keeping an eye on this 
system as it tracks into our area. Temperatures will continue to be 
pleasant into the weekend with highs most days in the mid to upper 
80s.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 639 AM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026

VFR CIGS through the forecast period. Expect a CU field after 15Z. 
Winds will be WNW at 8-12kts a few gusts are possible after 19Z. The 
CU field should clear after 00Z. Low confidence chances on TSRA 
after 06Z with a line of storms from the north.


//ATL Confidence...12Z Update...

Low on TSRA
High on all other elements.

Vaughn

Editorial #1 KAVL VFR Asheville Muni, NC, US · cool mountain escapeETE0h49Dist112 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KAVL observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

Editorial #13 KGKT VFR Gatlinburg-Pigeon Forge Arpt, TN, US · Smokies/GatlinburgETE0h50Dist114 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KGKT observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTYS is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHXD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KSAV is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Editorial #5 KMYR VFR Myrtle Beach Intl, SC, US · Myrtle Beach (Class C)ETE1h45Dist251 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KMYR observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

Editorial #15 KECP VFR Panama City/NW Florida Beaches Intl, FL, US · Panama City BeachETE1h38Dist237 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KECP observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

Editorial #21 KSPG VFR St Petersburg/Whitted Arpt, FL, US · St PetersburgETE2h35Dist379 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSPG observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KPIE is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KBFM observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

Editorial #26 KNEW VFR New Orleans/Lakefront Arpt, LA, US · New Orleans LakefrontETE2h38Dist389 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KNEW observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

Editorial #29 KBED LIFR Bedford/Hanscom Fld, MA, US · Boston-Bedford MAETE5h11Dist784 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KBED observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: out_of_window). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAM collection is not active for this run (state: UNCONFIGURED). Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

3 · Hazard feeds & regional observations

Unfiltered hazard feeds (not route-geometry screened): 10 SIGMET records, 32 G-AIRMET records, 1 CWA records. Regional current observations (not corridor forecasts): Gulf East: category unavailable at KTPF; Gulf West: category unavailable at KHSA; Long-range: IFR/LIFR at KBED; Long-range: MVFR at KHPN.
Scope: Hazard counts are raw feed totals and have not been filtered against a proposed route, altitude, or time. Airport flight categories are current point observations, not corridor forecasts.

4 · Planning gates

  • Evidence gate: an unavailable, stale, or out-of-horizon source is unknown — never treat it as favorable.
  • Weather gate: compare current observations and valid-period forecasts with personal ceiling, visibility, convection, wind, and crosswind minimums.
  • Route gate: screen the actual route, altitude, and time against official hazard products; feed totals on this page are not route-filtered.
  • Operations gate: verify NOTAMs, TFRs, runway conditions, fuel, aircraft performance, daylight, and alternates.

5 · ForeFlight manual cross-check (before flight)

  • ☐ Official briefing matches these go/no-go windows
  • ☐ Prog charts / radar / satellite trend agrees with convection timing
  • ☐ Winds & temps aloft along actual route (may shift ETE)
  • ☐ NOTAMs & TFRs — airport-scoped NMS records may be shown, but route-wide/TFR coverage is not included; pull a fresh official briefing for departure, destination, and alternates
  • ☐ Runway condition / length / closures at destination & alternate
  • ☐ Weight & balance + performance at forecast density altitude (heat!)
  • ☐ File & brief in ForeFlight; confirm fuel stops if long-range
